content: The FIGARO-DKD trial investigated the effects of finerenone, a nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA), on cardiovascular and renal outcomes in individuals with chronic kidney disease (CKD) and type 2 diabetes (T2D). This study enrolled 5,734 participants who had albuminuria and an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) ranging from 25 to 90 mL/min/1.73 m². Over a median follow-up period of 3.4 years, finerenone was shown to reduce the risk of major cardiovascular events—including cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, or hospitalization for heart failure—by 13% when compared to placebo. Additionally, finerenone significantly decreased the risk of end-stage kidney disease (ESKD) by 36% and reduced the likelihood of a sustained decline in eGFR from baseline by 57%.
